goodsIndustries.name: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing & Hunting
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting sector GDP fell 1.4% month-over-month in January 2026, the steepest monthly decline among the 20 NAICS industries, while holding +5.4% year-over-year, the strongest annual reading in the set.1 The U.S. Department of Commerce released preliminary results of the seventh administrative review of anti-dumping and countervailing duty orders on Canadian softwood lumber; BC Minister of Forests Ravi Parmar issued a response statement on April 9, 2026.2 Per NRCan, 66% of Canada's 2024 softwood lumber production was exported, approximately 90% of that to the United States.3

Canadian federal and provincial governments have announced more than C$2.1B in softwood lumber support over the past seven months, including a $1.2B BDC-backed Softwood Lumber Guarantee Program, Quebec's $60M wood-processing working capital top-up (March 2026), and a BC Stumpage Payment Deferral Program effective January 1, 2026.4 The project database tracks 17 agriculture and forestry projects ($5.47B), of which 13 forestry records (~$4.7B) fall within the scope of the U.S. DOC review and the Canadian support package.5 Nutrien (NTR) closed at $102.13, down 2.8% on the week, down 4.5% on the month, and up 56.5% year-over-year, registering against the Saskatchewan and Alberta potash records tracked in commodities.json.6

goodsIndustries.name: Mining, Quarrying & Oil/Gas Extraction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Mining, quarrying and oil/gas extraction sector GDP rose 1.2% month-over-month in January 2026 against a -0.1% year-over-year print.1 The Canadian Association of Energy Contractors projects an average of 213 active drilling rigs in 2026, up from 201 in 2025, with 5,709 wells forecast. The WTI 2026 strip averages approximately US$57/bbl, with the WCS differential at approximately US$12.80/bbl.2 The project database tracks 422 mining and energy projects ($268.74B).3

TC Energy and LNG Canada signed commercial agreements in March 2026 to advance Coastal GasLink Phase 2; capacity would expand from 2.1 Bcf/d to 5 Bcf/d via five new compressor stations, with final investment decision expected late 2026 or early 2027. LNG Canada Phase 1 completed in 2025 at approximately $40B; Phase 2 carries a $33B estimate and sits in the federal Major Projects Office portfolio.4 A March 2026 federal critical minerals package committed up to $165.2M for 22 projects, unlocking $434M across eight provinces, alongside a $1.5B First and Last Mile Fund and a $2B Critical Minerals Sovereign Fund.5 Cameco closed at $160.73, up 197.6% year-over-year; the URA ETF closed at $50.96, up 4.2% on the week. The Anglo-Teck merger of equals was announced at approximately US$57B.6

goodsIndustries.name: Utilities
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Utilities sector GDP rose 0.6% month-over-month in January 2026 against a -1.7% year-over-year print.1 Darlington unit 4 reconnected to the grid in March 2026, completing the C$12.8B refurbishment programme C$150M under budget and four months ahead of schedule. Ontario Power Generation's 300 MWe grid-scale SMR at Darlington is targeted for 2028 under the Canada SMR Action Plan.2 New Brunswick has committed to 600 MWe of new nuclear as part of a 2035 net-zero electricity plan, with a first SMR targeted for 2030 at Point Lepreau.3

The project database tracks 823 utilities projects ($522.77B), of which 14 energy storage records and 20 power plant records align with the SMR programme pipeline.4 Canada's grid is approximately 81% hydro, nuclear, wind and solar, and the Canadian Electricity Association estimates power demand could rise approximately 40% by 2050.5 The URA ETF closed at $50.96, up 4.2% on the week and 135.7% year-over-year, linking to the Saskatchewan uranium mine and SMR supply chain tagged in commodities.json as affecting SK, ON and NB.6 The TSX infrastructure basket closed at $56.38, up 0.5% on the week and 45.2% year-over-year, a market valuation proxy that registers against the 823-project NAICS 22 set.6

goodsIndustries.name: Construction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Construction sector GDP rose 1.1% month-over-month in January 2026 and 2.8% year-over-year, the only goods-producing NAICS with both prints positive.1 February 2026 housing starts registered 250,900 SAAR, up 4.5% from January's 240,148 SAAR and below the 252,500 consensus.2 GlobalData projects Canadian construction output +2.2% in 2025 and +2.6% in 2026, while projecting nonresidential starts -7.8% in 2026 as industrial (peaked 2024) and commercial (peaked 2025) segments normalize.3

Steel, as proxied by the SLX ETF, closed at $98.57, up 6.6% on the week, 6.0% on the month and 76.3% year-over-year, the largest weekly move of any construction input in the tracked commodity basket.4 The project database tracks 2,076 construction projects ($257.25B), with the largest concentrations in infrastructure (745 records), water and wastewater (578), and transit and rail (350).5 BC Minister of Housing Christine Boyle issued March 2026 housing highlights on April 10, 2026 and the April 2026 rental report statement on April 9, 2026; the policy tracker tags 114 BC projects as within the scope of those housing-eligible sectors.6 If February housing starts (250,900 SAAR) continue, they would register against the 157 residential and 60 housing project records tracked in the database.

goodsIndustries.name: Manufacturing
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Manufacturing sector GDP fell 1.4% month-over-month in January 2026 and 4.6% year-over-year, the largest annual decline of any goods-producing NAICS.1 Prime Minister Carney launched a new auto strategy on February 5, 2026, combining a $3B Strategic Response Fund for projects above $20M with up to $100M in a Regional Tariff Response Initiative.2 After approximately one year of U.S. auto tariffs, Canadian auto production has fallen from approximately 3 million vehicles in 2000 to approximately 1.3 million in 2025, and a February 2026 KPMG survey found 82% of Canadian manufacturers and suppliers are adjusting supply-chain strategies.3

The project database tracks 53 manufacturing projects ($67.39B).4 Ontario EV battery plant activity includes Volkswagen St. Thomas ($7B, PowerCo, operations 2027); Stellantis NextStar Windsor ($5B, 450,000 vehicles per year, online 2026); and Honda Alliston ($15B, four plants, postponed May 2025). Canada will allow up to 49,000 Chinese-made EVs per year at the MFN 6.1% rate.5 Steel input costs (SLX ETF) closed at $98.57, up 6.6% on the week and 76.3% year-over-year; nickel (NIKL ETF proxy) held flat at $28.40, linking to ON, QC, NL and MB EV battery supply-chain records.6
